chunks: Al-Sayyid al-Murtada allocated twelve dinars for him every month, from which he managed his livelihood.

key_terms.السَّيِّدُ الْمُرْتَضَى: al-Sharīf al-Murtaḍā — senior Shia theologian, jurist and poet (d. 436 AH), teacher of Shaykh al-Ṭūsī
key_terms.تَدْبِيرُ مَعَاشِهِ: management of his livelihood — the arrangement of his daily material sustenance and household needs
key_terms.دِينَارًا: dinar — Abbasid-era gold currency unit used as the standard measure of wealth

ai.seo_question: How did Sayyid al-Murtada financially support Shaykh al-Tusi with a monthly stipend of twelve dinars?
ai.summary: This biographical note records that Sayyid al-Murtada (ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Mūsawī, known as al-Sharīf al-Murtaḍā or ʿAlam al-Hudā, d. 436 AH/1044 CE) provided a monthly stipend of twelve dinars to Shaykh al-Ṭūsī (Shaykh al-Ṭāʾifa), his most distinguished student, to cover his living expenses. The passage reflects the tradition of scholarly patronage in early 5th-century AH Baghdad, where senior scholars and notables financially sustained gifted students to enable full devotion to learning.
